messages.subject: Suggestions for better plot
parts:

messages.subject: Remove legened?
parts:
I am trying to remove the Legend completely from a plot.
The last version of the GGplot book I have is last year and sections 6 &
8 give some details on the manipulation of titles and legends.
I have tried this and it does remove the name, key etc. but still has
the colored boxes for a legend.
So what is the syntax to remove the entire legend box from a plot?

legend.key = theme_blank(),legend.background = theme_blank(),
legend.title = theme_blank(), legend.text = theme_blank())

--
Bruce W. Miller, Ph.D.
Conservation Ecologist
Neotropical Bat Project

messages.subject: Re: Remove legened?
parts:
Hi Bruce,

Adding this layer to your plot will do it:

 +opts(legend.position = "none")


-AC

On Fri, Dec 11, 2009 at 17:47, Bruce Miller <bats...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I have 3 Excel charts that i would like to combine and I think with selecting the correct faceting this can be accomplished so the output is one plot (graphic) with stacked plots.  In Excel the data tables are broken into three months and the values are a "relative abundance" for each critter listed.  A sample Excel plot is at the bottom but I am trying to set this up with GGPlot2 so the Y axis is the same for all 3 months for comparison.  I have been away form GGPLOT  since May and trying to get back up to speed.

You first need everything in one data.frame. So add a month column and
rbind() your datasets. Then you need geom_bar() with position="dodge".
See : http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_bar.html

JiHO
